newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA PM EXPECTS LOCAL FUNDS TO BUY STOCKS SOON.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA PM EXPECTS LOCAL FUNDS TO BUY STOCKS SOON.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday he expects local funds to start buying stocks soon.
"I expect local funds to come in. If I were a player, I would come in and buy," Mahathir told reporters when asked about the prospects for the local stock market.
"Big funds should come in because they could get a bargain," he said.

Share prices on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange have fallen by 7.4 percent to 928.33 points after the announcement of a $2.0 million limit on non-trade currency swaps by local banks with foreigners and a 2.8 billion ringgit trade deficit for June.
"I am not worried. It is usual for fund managers to pull out at such times because they are afraid of bad times," Mahathir said when asked about the sharp fall.
When asked how long the restriction on swaps will stay in place, Mahathir said, "As long as it is necessary."
"It is not a restriction but (creating) a differential rate of interest," he said.
The new ruling on swaps creates a two-tier interest rate market, one offshore and the other onshore, by restricting acccess to ringgit.

Mahathir said he was concerned with the sharp fall in the ringgit. When told that most major currencies of the world had eased against the U.S. dollar, including the German deutschemark, he said, "I think the Germans can afford it, we can't. Five percent decline is a big loss for us."
"That's why I suggest they should attack the big currencies. They should attack the U.S. dollar, for example," he said.
But, he sidestepped questions on the ringgit's level against the dollar that the government would consider comfortable.
The ringgit has in the last two months fallen to three-year lows. On Thursday evening, it was at 2.6450 to a dollar against 2.50 around one month ago.
